result.summary: Phase 2 of #221 (E4-XML RC-Dynamik) wires 4 previously-inert Resource-Control axes from the ComdareResourceControlV1 POD through to their organs so they take real runtime effect at the multi-day #156 measurement run (previously only prefetch_distance was wired; the other 4 were stored in applied_rc_ but never reached an organ, producing "Phantom-Zeilen"). The substance is in the ce commit 1f9c2eef (12 files, +548/-44): libs/cache_engine/anatomy/abi_adapter.hpp gains 4 new `if constexpr (requires { organ_.set_runtime_X(...); })` application blocks mirroring the existing prefetch_distance pattern, and five organ headers gain the matching runtime setters + drive logic — axis_08_concurrency_observable.hpp (set_runtime_thread_count driving repeated acquire/release pairs), axis_04_node_type_layout_aware_store.hpp (set_runtime_pool_budget_bytes plus reworked copy/move ctors), observable_composed_container.hpp and observable_composed_search.hpp (set_runtime_batch_size + pool_budget delegation and drive_runtime_batch_probe_), and axis_14_value_handle_observable.hpp (set_runtime_inline_threshold_bytes). A new DEG test tests/unit/test_221_rc_remaining_axes.cpp (+215) is added and registered via tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt (+20), and four builder CMakeLists.txt swap CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR->PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR. The super commit 2a8c36c is a one-line submodule pointer bump advancing Code/external/comdare-cache-engine from fc6f2e4 to exactly the reviewed ce sha 1f9c2ee. Note: the review target's prose omitted tests/unit/CMakeLists.txt from its enumerated file list, but it is the 12th changed file (test registration).

candidates.summary: restore_statistics replaced `{ stats_ = s; }` (whose invariant was: restore observable state EXACTLY to the passed save-Stand snapshot) with a body that ZEROES runtime_batch_probe_count_/checksum instead of restoring them, because snapshot_t (SearchAlgoStatistics) carries no batch-probe field — the exact-restore invariant is not re-established for the new counters.
candidates.failure_scenario: At the #156 hard-gate a batch_size>0 tier is measured via the preferred CoW two-phase harness: tier_save_all saves container_algorithm_.statistics() (SearchAlgoStatistics has no batch-probe member, confirmed at axis_03a_search_algo_cache_engine_permutation_concept.hpp:45) and tier_rollback_all (abi_adapter.hpp:1719) calls restore_statistics. restore_statistics zeroes runtime_batch_probe_count_ rather than restoring the checkpoint value — and in the materialized-write branch it overwrites the value the full copy-assignment at abi_adapter.hpp:1706 had already restored correctly. If any batch-probing lookup ran before the checkpoint (warmup not stat-reset), the first measured iteration exports axis_stats[0][7]=C0+delta while every later iteration exports only delta, so the traversal batch-probe signal that #221 exists to produce is non-reproducible/undercounted across CoW iterations. The identical defect is in observable_composed_container.hpp:157.

candidates.summary: append_slot gained a budget-rejection early-return (line 203), but rebuild_ (line 467, called by erase_slot_at/insert_slot_at/migrate) still relies on the old invariant that append_slot ALWAYS appends the given slot to faithfully reconstruct the flattened set; that append-always guarantee is now conditional and not re-established in rebuild_.
candidates.failure_scenario: A tier whose pool_budget_bytes is nonzero and whose live set already exceeds that budget (budget applied/lowered after records were loaded — the guard blocks growth, never shrink) receives an erase: erase_slot_at (line 231) flattens all slots, then rebuild_ does clear() (size_->0) and re-appends via append_slot, which now early-returns as soon as capacity_bytes_for_slot_count_ crosses the budget. Every slot past the budget is silently discarded, so erasing one key drops other still-valid keys — subsequent tier_lookup of those keys returns miss (wrong result / data loss) and tier_size undercounts, corrupting the #156 workload state.

candidates.summary: observe_value_handle replaced the unconditional `has_version_tag_()` version-tag counting and `chain_depth_()` depth with effective_has_version_tag_() (false whenever runtime_inline_threshold_bytes_!=0) and effective_chain_depth_() (1 or 2, ignoring the strategy's compile-time chain_depth_), removing the version-tag/chain-depth accounting for the entire RC-override path.
candidates.failure_scenario: At #156 a tier composed with a versioned-pointer (or multi-level chain) value_handle AND a nonzero inline_threshold_bytes RC: version_tag_strips is gated on effective_has_version_tag_() which returns false for any threshold!=0, and depth comes from effective_chain_depth_() which collapses to 1 or 2 regardless of the strategy's real chain_depth_. The versioned/chained strategy therefore reports version_tag_strips=0 (axis_stats[11][2]) and a collapsed peak_chain_depth/indirect_deref_count for the whole inline_threshold sweep, hiding the MVCC/chain work the T11 value-handle axis is supposed to measure — a phantom-zero introduced in a different axis by the RC wiring.

candidates.summary: The new pool-budget guard lives inside the shared append_slot primitive (line 204), so unguarded rebuild_-based callers (erase_slot_at line 234, organ_migrate_step line 362) silently drop live records when the budget is below current occupancy.
candidates.failure_scenario: Apply a pool_budget_bytes smaller than a populated tier's current occupancy (the setter does not clamp and the commit's own doc states existing chunks are not reclaimed, so size_ > budget-capacity is reachable). Erasing any single key runs erase_slot_at -> rebuild_ (line 469), which clear()s then re-appends every survivor through the now-guarded append_slot; each survivor beyond the budget capacity is silently discarded and increments runtime_pool_budget_rejections_, which feeds allocator_statistics().failure_count (line 248). A one-key erase thus destroys many other live records and emits a burst of phantom allocator-failure counts, corrupting both the stored data and the T6 allocator measurement at #156.

candidates.summary: thread_count is modeled as N sequential acquire/release pairs in a single thread, scaling acquire/release counts by N while contention/validation stay 0.
candidates.failure_scenario: With thread_count=3, observe_critical_section runs 3 sequential lock/unlock pairs, so axis_stats[8][0]/[8][1] (acquire/release) scale x3 but axis_stats[8][2]/[8][3] (contention/validation_fail) remain 0. The T8 output at #156 therefore describes a physically impossible '3 concurrent threads with zero contention'; any thesis interpretation of thread_count as real concurrency, or of contention-per-acquire, is misled by a purely sequential repetition dressed up as parallelism.

The deterministic counter outputs axis_stats[0][0..7] (abi_adapter.hpp:1040-1051) and the golden/checksum fixtures are byte-identical at RC=0, so golden-neutrality (the review target's parenthetical meaning of 'byte-identical') holds; the candidate itself concedes the timing effect is 'uniform across RC=0 rows (cancels in comparisons)'. So the impact is a negligible, canceling, branch-predicted timing perturbation whose materiality is uncertain and, by the finding's own admission, immaterial to the scientific comparisons. WHY NOT REFUTED: the branch is factually present on the actual timed member path (not optimizable away there), so it is not 'no observable effect' in principle, and the review target explicitly asked to flag 'extra branches on the hot path'. Confirming a real defect would require showing the timing offset is non-uniform or that a measured/golden value actually differs at RC=0 — neither is present.

The divergence is real in code: restore_statistics (observable_composed_search.hpp / _container.hpp) does `stats_ = s; reset_runtime_batch_probe_statistics();` (zeros runtime_batch_probe_count_/checksum_), while the twin restore_state does `runtime_batch_probe_count_ = m.runtime_batch_probe_count;` (restores). abi_adapter.hpp cow path: line 1706 `if (cow_materialized_) container_algorithm_ = *saved_container_algorithm_` (full-wrapper copy incl. counters) then line 1719 `container_algorithm_.restore_statistics(...)` re-zeros them; the fallback memento path at line 1730 `container_algorithm_.restore_state(...)` restores them. So `cow_capable_ compositions -> batch_probe_count==0 after rollback` is CONFIRMED (line 1719 always runs in the cow path). BUT the distinctive claim — that a DIFFERENT class of compositions (`memento-path compositions retain the saved value`) coexists, making the DEG diverge purely on cow_capable_ — has an unconfirmed trigger: cow_capable_ (abi_adapter.hpp:2106-2108) = organ_cow_capable_v && is_copy_constructible && is_copy_assignable, and the memento path (line 1730) is only reached when container_algorithm_t is NON-copy-assignable but MementoAxis. The batch-bearing organs are ObservableComposedSearch/-Container, and the reworked axis_04 LayoutAwareChunkedStore retains BOTH copy-ctor and copy-assignment (fully copy-assignable) -> cow-capable; I could not confirm any #156 batch-bearing composition whose container_algorithm_t is non-copy-assignable-but-MementoAxis. If all such compositions are cow-capable, they all zero uniformly (no cross-composition divergence, though the undercount of [1] still holds). What would confirm: a #156 composition whose container_algorithm_ routes through abi_adapter.hpp:1730 (restore_state).

restore_statistics zeros the batch counters instead of restoring them: `void restore_statistics(snapshot_t const& s) noexcept { stats_ = s; reset_runtime_batch_probe_statistics(); }` where reset_runtime_batch_probe_statistics sets runtime_batch_probe_count_=0/checksum_=0 (observable_composed_search.hpp and _container.hpp) — contradicting its comment 'stellt im Zwei-Phasen-Rollback die Zaehler EXAKT auf den save-Stand zurueck' and diverging from save_state/restore_state which carry them through m.runtime_batch_probe_count. This runs in the two-phase cow rollback (abi_adapter.hpp:1719, the sole functional caller), which #156 executes per-op: perm_runner.hpp:273 calls run_workload_profile with rollback when rb_exact, and every op goes through ac::detail::two_phase_measure (tier_observe_trace_abi.hpp:113-117: save->warmup->rollback->measure; workload_orchestrator.hpp:78/91/106/146). Critically, a VALID row requires two-phase (perm_runner.hpp:251 `r.two_phase_valid = rb_exact`), so the bug corrupts exactly the rows that count. Failure: batch_size RC != 0 on a cow-capable composition. Each per-op rollback (line 1719) zeros runtime_batch_probe_count_ while restoring stats_ to the per-op save value; so at run-end tier.tier_observe (workload_orchestrator.hpp:162) reads axis_stats[0][7] = only the last probing op's probes (~batch_size) or 0, whereas axis_stats[0][0] (lookup_count, from restored+accumulated stats_) reaches N. The new test RcBatchSize221 pins the INTENDED accumulated value at `EXPECT_EQ(rc_snapshot.axis_stats[0][7], 15u)` (3 lookups x 5) but only via direct tier_lookup (no two_phase_measure), so it never catches the collapse — the batch_size axis would still read as a phantom (~0) at the #156 two-phase run, the very thing #221 set out to prevent.

candidates.summary: The #133 two-phase memento rollback restore_state() -- documented (lines 238-241) to restore the data substrate EXACTLY -- delegates to ComposedSearch::restore_state, which does store_.clear() (clear() at axis_04 line 236 does NOT reset runtime_pool_budget_bytes_) and then re-inserts every saved record via Traversal::insert_into -> append_slot/insert_slot_at, both now budget-gated; so under an active pool_budget RC the whole warm-state restore silently drops its tail. This is a different, more severe caller than the erase_slot_at/insert_slot_at/migrate paths already flagged: it is the loop's reset mechanism itself.
candidates.failure_scenario: The #156 RuntimeVariableLoop pre-loads a fixed tier with N records (as the test comment 'keeps the composition fixed and varies only RC' implies), takes save_state (memento = N records), then sweeps RC settings on the SAME tier: it applies pool_budget_bytes sized for only K<N records, measures, then calls restore_state to reset for the next setting. restore_state -> search_.restore_state -> store_.clear() (budget still active) -> re-insert N records, of which the N-K tail is budget-rejected. The store now permanently holds only K records, so every subsequent swept RC row is measured against a truncated substrate, corrupting the whole sweep.

candidates.summary: allocator_statistics() folds the pool-budget POLICY rejection count into the allocator snapshot's failure_count, which fill_observer_v3 (abi_adapter line 1123) exports as the T6 'fail' CSV column -- so a traversal/node pool_budget RC contaminates the genuine allocator-OOM-failure signal with policy rejections; and because clear() (line 236) never resets runtime_pool_budget_rejections_, the count accumulates monotonically across the tier's lifetime and is re-incremented by every over-budget restore_state re-insert, inflating 'fail' to an arbitrary multiple of the real rejection count.
candidates.failure_scenario: In a #156 run with pool_budget RC active, the 5th insert into a one-chunk-budget store is policy-rejected; allocator_statistics() returns failure_count=1 even though std::malloc never failed, and the T6 CSV 'fail' column reads 1 (a phantom allocator failure). Across repeated save/restore rollback cycles the rejection re-fires each cycle because clear() keeps runtime_pool_budget_rejections_, so 'fail' climbs cycle-by-cycle, making the allocator-failure metric unable to distinguish real allocator pressure from budget-policy denials -- a scientist reads it as allocator instability. The new DEG test never exercises multi-cycle accumulation, so it stays green.

verdicts.evidence: The candidate's low-level facts are accurate (composable_search.hpp:230-233 `restore_state` does `store_.clear()` + `Traversal::insert_into` re-insert; axis_04 `clear()` at line 236 leaves `runtime_pool_budget_bytes_` intact; append_slot/insert_slot_at are budget-gated at axis_04:204,223), but the premise that the #133 two-phase rollback / #156 loop reset delegates to `ComposedSearch::restore_state` is factually wrong. tier_rollback_all (abi_adapter.hpp:1727-1730): `if constexpr (std::is_copy_assignable_v<container_algorithm_t>) { ... container_algorithm_ = *saved_container_algorithm_; } else if constexpr (MementoAxis<...>) container_algorithm_.restore_state(...)` — restore_state is only the ELSE branch, reachable solely for NON-copy-assignable containers; the CoW path (line 1706) also copy-assigns. The budget gate exists ONLY in LayoutAwareChunkedStore (grep: only axis_04 implements runtime_pool_budget_can_grow_by_one; observable_composed_search/container merely probe it via `if constexpr(requires...)`). LayoutAwareChunkedStore is copy-constructible AND copy-assignable (axis_04:141-179) and its copy_from_ copies runtime_pool_budget_bytes_ + chunk buffers byte-for-byte (axis_04:529-543,541), so every budget-gated container is copy-assignable and cow_capable_ (abi_adapter:2106-2108) — the copy-assignment branch is statically selected and the restore_state re-insert path is `if constexpr`-excluded; rollback restores the store byte-for-byte, dropping no tail. Additionally the real dynamic RC sweep never uses save/restore: RuntimeVariableLoop (runtime_variable_loop.hpp:73-107) applies RC per setting then calls the visitor; HostMeasureLoop (host_measure_loop.hpp:40-70) does insert/lookup/observe with no save_state/restore_state; the new unit test resets via tier_clear + fresh insert (test_221 lines 903-911), not restore_state. The hypothesized 'save_state once, restore_state between settings' loop does not exist in the code.

axis_04_node_type_layout_aware_store.hpp:248 (new in 1f9c2ee): `if constexpr (requires { s.failure_count; }) s.failure_count += runtime_pool_budget_rejections_;` adds a POLICY counter to the allocator snapshot's failure_count. failure_count is a genuine real-OOM signal: axis_06_allocator_mimalloc.hpp:139 and axis_06_allocator_std_malloc.hpp:114 do `++stats_.failure_count` ONLY when `p == nullptr`. The value reaches the T6 'fail' CSV column: observable_composed_search.hpp:159 delegates store_allocator_statistics()->store().allocator_statistics(); abi_adapter.hpp:1123 `r[4] = a.failure_count` -> axis_stats[6][4] -> alloc_failure_count (result_ingest.hpp:76) -> CSV header `...dealloc_cnt;fail;` (cache_engine_builder_iterator.hpp:214, value :369). LayoutAwareChunkedStore is the measured store for the search_algo axes (linear_scan/k_ary/interpolation registry). The committed DEG test test_221_rc_remaining_axes.cpp:152-162 sets pool_budget_bytes=one chunk with al::StdMalloc (line 62, never returns null), rejects the 5th insert (append_slot line 204-206 -> note_runtime_pool_budget_rejection()), and asserts EXPECT_GT(snapshot.axis_stats[6][4], 0u): the 'fail' column reads 1 while malloc never failed = phantom allocator failure. clear() (lines 236-241) does NOT reset runtime_pool_budget_rejections_, and reset_axis_statistics_() (abi_adapter 1881-1903, called by tier_reset_statistics) does not touch it either, so the contribution is sticky across the tier lifetime; rebuild_() (467-470)->clear()->append_slot() re-checks budget and can re-fire rejections. Contamination + non-reset are fully confirmed with quoted lines and demonstrated by the project's own test; the 'arbitrary multiple across save/restore cycles' magnitude is a plausible amplifier resting on a repeated over-budget re-populate loop I did not fully trace, but the core measurement-integrity defect for #156 is confirmed.

result.summary: Max-effort review of the Phase-2 commit that wires four resource-control axes (batch_size, pool_budget_bytes, thread_count, inline_threshold_bytes) into the #156 measurement; the 29 verified findings collapse to 15 distinct defects. The gravest are correctness/measurement-integrity bugs: silent data loss when a lowered pool budget makes erase/migrate re-append survivors through the now budget-gated append_slot; budget-rejected non-stored inserts still driving every sibling organ so multiple axes over-count; and the flagship batch_size axis broken four independent ways (container for_each_record full-scan that never stops at batch_size, restore_statistics zeroing the probe counters on two-phase rollback, the counters written to nullptr CSV-schema columns so they never reach the output, and masstree silently no-oping without for_each_record). The remainder are the 0-as-sentinel RC latch that prevents returning any axis to default on a reused tier, allocator failure_count contamination with policy rejections, config-gated distortions (pool_budget not applied to pool-family organs, value_handle version/chain-depth suppressed under RC) plus two latent divide-by-zero paths, and low-severity cleanups (write-only checksum/DCE risk, extra hot-path branch).
